implemented_capabilities.capability: Bounded read-only graph retrieval (search, neighbours, multi-hop paths, subgraph, timeline)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Parameterised Cypher with depth clamped to 1..4 and limits clamped to config.MAX_QUERY_RESULTS; the only string interpolation is a clamped integer path depth. Variable-length undirected traversal with LIMIT, no weights.

implemented_capabilities.capability: What-if outage blast radius over DEPENDS_ON
implemented_capabilities.notes: Real Cypher MATCH (downstream:System)-[:DEPENDS_ON*1..3]->(target) giving hop counts and paths, but the risk tier and 'estimated_cascade_seconds' (15/35/60) are hard-coded constants, with special-casing on substrings 'SYS-AUTH'/'SYS-GATEWAY'.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Cross-session investigation memory with context reuse
implemented_capabilities.notes: Persists Session/Investigation/Finding/Evidence nodes with REVISITS and DERIVED_FROM edges and finds prior sessions by target or 1-2 hop neighbours. CONTRADICTED_PRIOR_FINDING is declared in REUSE_STATUSES but never returned; every evidence item is attached to every finding (nested loop, memory_service.py:96-148). Prior-session matching uses CONTAINS on JSON strings.

Small, honest data model: claim, source_records, graph_path, rule_id, epistemic_type (STORED_FACT/RULE_BASED_INFERENCE/HYPOTHESIS), sufficiency, missing_evidence. Only 4 hand-written rules; no automatic rule evaluation.

Regex intent routing, then if-branches keyed on the literal seeded IDs E-101/E-102 that emit pre-written claims and findings (agent.py:121-167). Graph calls are real but conclusions are hard-coded for the demo dataset.
Four rounds of pre-written f-string text; consensus_confidence 0.92, 'VERIFIED_ROOT_CAUSE' and 'EVT-0945' are constants (debate_service.py:34-94). No LLM, no logic.
Three canned runbook templates with kubectl/helm/redis-cli/curl strings, claims '100% EXECUTABLE_SRE_RUNBOOK'. Commands are returned as data, never executed.
Real CREATE of Event/Record nodes linked AFFECTS to a System from Prometheus/Datadog-style payload, then calls the scripted agent.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Scripted v1 API for the Next.js UI
implemented_capabilities.notes: /api/v1/investigate returns hard-coded investigation payloads (risk scores, reasoning steps) based on whether the entity id contains 'E-102' or 'SQL'; graph/entities/sessions routes are partly live, the rest are in-memory demo lists.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Localhost TCP bridge Windows<->WSL for FalkorDB
implemented_capabilities.notes: Dev-environment workaround (TCP relay with worker pool); has no relevance to Kairos and contains hard-coded host paths/IPs.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels (schema.py NODE_LABELS): Person, User, Organization, Project, System, Software, Event, Record, Document, Task, Session, Conversation, Message, Fact, Entity, Evidence, Decision, Investigation, Finding. Edges: DEPENDS_ON, USES, AFFECTS, LED_TO, RECORDED_IN, SUPPORTED_BY, DERIVED_FROM, REVISITS, DISCOVERED_IN, OWNS, HAS_CONVERSATION, HAS_MESSAGE, HAS_FACT, MENTIONS, etc. Index syntax CREATE INDEX ON :Label(prop) (older style; FalkorDB 4.x accepts it). Variable-length undirected paths [r*1..N], no APOC/GDS. Single graph 'contextgraph' with no tenant separation.
algorithms: Bounded variable-length path trace between two ids (graph_queries.py:build_multi_hop_query, depth 1..4)
Downstream transitive closure over DEPENDS_ON up to 3 hops with hop-count bucketing (whatif_simulator.py:simulate_system_outage)
Prior-session reuse by 1-2 hop connected entity match (memory_service.py:evaluate_context_reuse)
backend_interfaces: MCP stdio server mcp_server.py (search_entities, get_entity_details, find_related_records, trace_multi_hop_relationships, retrieve_previous_context, reconstruct_incident_timeline, run_agent_investigation, simulate_what_if_outage, generate_mitigation_runbook, run_dual_agent_debate, ingest_monitoring_alert)
frontend_interfaces: Next.js pages: investigation, graph, sessions, scenarios, health, explainability, comparison
Components: InteractiveGraph.tsx, NodeInspector.tsx, EdgeInspector.tsx, AgentTimeline.tsx, EvidenceDrawer.tsx, CrossSessionInsightCard.tsx, FloatingAssistant.tsx, HolographicGraphStage.tsx
lib/api/apiClient.ts with demo-mode fallback and lib/demo/*.ts static data
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Cross-session memory stored in FalkorDB: Session -OWNS-> Investigation -DISCOVERED_IN-> Finding -SUPPORTED_BY-> Evidence, Session -REVISITS-> earlier Session, Finding -DERIVED_FROM-> Finding. Chat turns persisted as User/Conversation/Message nodes. Agent is deterministic (no LLM by default); optional Ollama text generation grounded on retrieved graph context (chat_service.py:_query_ollama). No state machine, handoffs, or approval flow.
tests_present: 9 pytest files under tests/ (~47 test functions: test_agent, test_e2e_demo, test_evidence, test_graph_queries, test_master_features, test_mcp, test_memory, test_simulation, test_unique_features). Integration tests that require a live seeded FalkorDB (e.g. assert nodes>0).
security_findings: server.py:37 - CORSMiddleware allow_origins=['*']; no authentication on any route including destructive /api/memory DELETE and simulation reset
falkordb_bridge.py:57 - control listener binds 0.0.0.0:6382 with no authentication; any LAN host can register as a worker and receive proxied FalkorDB traffic
falkordb_bridge.py:28-35 - subprocess.Popen of 'wsl -u root -d Ubuntu -- python3 /mnt/d/PROJECT/ai-agent/wsl_bridge_agent.py' (hard-coded path, root user)
wsl_bridge_agent.py:11 - hard-coded Windows host IP 172.31.80.1 and unauthenticated socket relay to FalkorDB 127.0.0.1:6379

remediation_service.py:117,125,133,138 - f-strings embed user-supplied entity id into shell commands (journalctl/consul/kubectl) and into a Cypher string (MATCH (n {id: '{clean_id}'})); returned as data, not executed, but unsafe if a consumer runs them
remediation_service.py:59 - canned redis-cli EVAL that deletes keys 'auth:sig:*' presented as an executable runbook step
chat_service.py:611 - outbound httpx POST to config.OLLAMA_BASE_URL (env-controlled, no allowlist)
webhook_service.py:48-105 - unauthenticated alert ingestion creates graph nodes from arbitrary payload (graph poisoning), triggers agent run
config.py:12-40 - FalkorDB password read from env/REDIS_URL; no hard-coded secrets found. No eval/exec/pickle found.
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps incident/root-cause investigation, dependency blast-radius traversal (whatif_simulator), agent session memory/provenance (memory_service/evidence_service) and software-vulnerability correlation (Record -AFFECTS-> Software <-USES- System).
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - defines an Evidence/Finding/Session provenance model with epistemic types, sufficiency levels, missing-evidence lists and REVISITS/DERIVED_FROM links, but contradiction/invalidation (CONTRADICTED_PRIOR_FINDING) is declared and never implemented and nothing is temporal or approval-gated.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Compact, readable schema for evidence records (claim, rule, epistemic_type, sufficiency, missing_evidence, source_session_id) and prior-context lookup that could seed an Evidence Drift evidence node model; the traversal and what-if Cypher in graph_queries.py/whatif_simulator.py are simple and portable.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB only (no LLM key; Ollama optional)

strategy_rationale: Most of the 'intelligence' (agent findings, debate, runbooks, v1 API) is hard-coded around two seeded events, so the code should not be merged. Use the evidence/epistemic data model and the bounded traversal Cypher as design reference for Kairos.
